dossier.summary: Orchard Mechanical is a commercial HVAC and plumbing contractor with about 140 people across two branches in Ohio. It runs service and install crews out of both branches and dispatches around 40 technicians a day.
dossier.why_now: Posted three dispatcher openings in October 2026.

data.title: How Orchard's dispatchers could stop rebuilding the board every morning
data.intro: Three dispatcher openings in one quarter usually means the board is rebuilt by hand every morning. Here is what I would look at first at Orchard, and what I would leave alone.

reasons.heading: Three dispatcher openings in one quarter
reasons.body: That is a lot of hiring for a team your size. Most of the time it points to work the board should be doing for the dispatchers, like reshuffling the day when a job runs long.

reasons.heading: Two branches, one set of technicians
reasons.body: Your service and install crews run out of both Ohio branches. When each branch keeps its own board, a technician who is free in one branch is invisible to the other.

reasons.heading: Service and install on the same day
reasons.body: Around 40 technicians a day across service calls and installs is where a shared spreadsheet starts to slip. I would start with the service side, because that is where a missed callback shows up first.
